steps.body: Fractions over 10 or over 100 convert straight to decimals: the denominator names the place, the numerator fills it.
steps.narration: Fractions over 10 or over 100 convert straight to decimals: the denominator names the place, the numerator fills it.

widget.prompt: Shade the grid to show 0.53. Each full column is one tenth; each cell is one hundredth.

commonCounts.feedback: That shades only 3 single cells. The tenths digit of 0.53 is worth whole columns: 5 full columns first, then 3 more cells.
That count swaps the digits of 0.53. The first digit after the point counts full columns; the second counts single cells.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly 53 of the 100 cells — 5 full columns and 3 more cells: 53 hundredths, written 0.53.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is still below the target. Fill whole columns for the tenths digit first, then single cells for the hundredths.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount has gone past the target. Each full column is one tenth — check the tenths digit before adding single cells.

predict.prompt: The fraction 53/100 will be shaded on the grid. Which decimal names it?
predict.reveal: 53 of 100 equal parts is 53 hundredths — the decimal places that count two digits after the point: 0.53. A bare 53 would mean 53 whole grids, not 53 parts of one.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g4d fraction to decimal.

misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g4d fraction to decimal.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: A denominator of 100 names hundredths, so the numerator fills that place.

widget.prompt: Write the fraction 53/100 as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: That drops the denominator. The fraction names 53 parts out of 100, so its decimal must end in the hundredths place — a value less than one whole.
That treats the count as tenths, naming 53/10 instead. A denominator of 100 means the count must end two places after the decimal point.

widget.fallbackFeedback: A denominator of 100 means hundredths. Write the numerator so its last digit lands two places after the decimal point.

hints: Hundredths: two places after the point.

widget.prompt: Write the fraction 8/10 as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: That drops the denominator. The fraction names 8 parts out of 10, so its decimal puts the 8 in the tenths place — a value less than one whole.
That writes 8 in the hundredths place, which names 8/100. Tenths sit one place higher: directly after the decimal point.

widget.fallbackFeedback: A denominator of 10 means tenths. Write the numerator in the tenths place, directly after the decimal point.
